newsitem.title: UK: New classification scheme for British hotels.
newsitem.headline: New classification scheme for British hotels.

text.p: The English Tourist Board (ETB) and motoring organisations the AA and the RAC have agreed a harmonised scheme for the rating of hotels, the ETB said in a statement on Monday.

The new scheme, based on the internationally recognised one-five star rating, replaces three different systems run by the different organisations. The scheme will be run in England by the ETB and across Britain by the AA and RAC.
It is hoped that it will end customer confusion and provide a further boost to the tourism industry.
The rankings will be based on quality requirements as well as a judgement on facilities and services.
North of the border, the Scottish Tourist Board plans to continue using its own-star system, based solely on the quality of what is provided.
The Wales Tourist Board is expected eventually to join the move towards harmonisation.
The Scottish and Welsh bodies have agreed to participate fully with the ETB, RAC and AA in running a separate star system for "Bed and Breakfasts", guesthouses and inns.
